newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's capital city shaken by small earthquake.
newsitem.headline: NZ's capital city shaken by small earthquake.

text.p: An earthquake shook Wellington on Sunday morning but was too minor to cause any damage, Radio New Zealand reported.
Seismologists said the quake measured 4.5 on the Richter scale and was recorded at 8.53 a.m. (1953 GMT).
They said the quake was centred 35 km (23 miles) north of Wellington out to sea and was reasonably shallow.
Wellington resident John Hathoway told Radio New Zealand the quake began sharply.
"The whole place shuddered and then it rolled, and the rolling business was really quite noticeable. It was the sort of earthquake that you couldn't ignore," he said. It lasted about five seconds.
